discrepancies: School return is conditional on symptoms/contact risk and clinician guidance, not a universal antibiotic prerequisite.
Steroid-antibiotic combinations need a diagnosed steroid-responsive indication; not routine undifferentiated conjunctivitis therapy.
Ozurdex is an intravitreal implant, not a surface eye drop.
Mild versus severe inflammation alone does not select NSAID versus steroid; indication and corneal/infection risks govern.

Contact-lens intervals, product spacing, preparation, drop count, storage and discard instructions are formulation-specific. Preservative-free products can still burn and may be single-use or multidose.

Current systemic CDC neonatal and adult gonococcal/chlamydial pathways supersede legacy topical-label implications. Ceftriaxone neonatal label versus guidance differences are disclosed with specialist resolution.
Older availability listings are qualified; FDA 2026 Orange Book confirms Alomide discontinued. Historical formulations are not current supply recommendations.
PDE5/NAION temporal association is not established causation. Ocular medication injury is not uniformly reversible.
AAO 2025 retinal screening revision supersedes older screening simplifications; severe-obesity abstract/full-text wording is documented.
Systane, Clear Eyes and bromfenac structured strength anomalies are resolved against product labeling, with conversions recorded.
numericalValidation: Neonatal erythromycin: 3.2 kg x 50 mg/kg/day / 4 = 40 mg per dose.
Systane propylene glycol 0.6% = 6 mg/mL; Clear Eyes naphazoline 0.012% = 0.12 mg/mL and glycerin 0.25% = 2.5 mg/mL.
Bromfenac 0.09% free acid = 0.9 mg/mL; salt-equivalent labeling must not be misread as free-acid strength.
Cross-module HCQ calculations: 68 x 5 = 340 mg/day; 400/60 = 6.6667 mg/kg/day and 60 x 5 = 300 mg/day.
